decisions.reason: The quote explicitly mentions 'decreased neurodegeneration' in CLN2 knock-out mice (BD mouse model). While the quote shows treatment reduced neurodegeneration, the surrounding abstract establishes that CLN2 BD is characterized by progressive loss of neurological functions, and the quote describes neurodegeneration as a phenotype that is ameliorated by treatment. This clearly establishes that neurodegeneration is a phenotype of CLN2 disease.

The quote explicitly mentions 'decreased neuroinflammation' in CLN2 knock-out mice (BD mouse model). The presence of neuroinflammation in untreated CLN2 mice establishes neuroinflammation as a phenotype of CLN2 disease that can be reduced by treatment.

The quote refers to 'reduced aggregation of lysosomal storage material' in CLN2 knock-out mice. The opening of the abstract states CLN2 BD 'is characterized by...a build-up of toxic intracellular storage material in all organs.' The quote describing accumulation/aggregation of lysosomal storage material in the disease model establishes this as a phenotype of CLN2 disease.

The quote states 'A combination of intrathecal and intraperitoneal EV-TPP1 injections significantly prolonged lifespan in BD mice.' BD mice are established in the abstract as CLN2 knock-out mice (CLN2 disease model). Significantly prolonging lifespan is a therapeutic effect that treats the disease. The relationship is established but inferred from the extended lifespan outcome.

The quote demonstrates multiple therapeutic effects of EV-TPP1 in CLN2 knock-out mice (BD model): decreased neurodegeneration, decreased neuroinflammation, and reduced lysosomal storage material aggregation. These are therapeutic effects on CLN2 disease phenotypes. The evidence clearly supports that EV-TPP1 has therapeutic effects on CLN2 disease.
